voyage.name: White Night Festival
voyage.content: This annual event is a celebration of Tel Aviv's White City's proclamation as a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage Site and organized by Tel Aviv's municipality. During the "White Night", cultural institutions, as well as commercial ones, are open to the public all night long, and many special events take place. In the past it usually took place late June or early July.

voyage.name: Tel Aviv Fashion Market
voyage.content: A highly recommended biannual event (winter/summer, for three days each time) where Tel Aviv's top clothing designers show and sell their stuff. Focused on urban clothing. Don't miss this colorful carnival of cutting-edge fashion!

voyage.name: Night Flea
voyage.content: Every August, Jaffa's burgeoning flea market is active all through the night on weekends, with special events, shows and exhibitions taking place.

voyage.name: Docaviv
voyage.address: The Tel Aviv Cinematheque, 2 Shprintzak St
voyage.content: Tel Aviv's International Documentary Film Festival. Every year in May, Docaviv presents the most innovative, provocative and important documentary films of the year from around the world.

voyage.name: The Tel Aviv International LGBT Film Festival
voyage.address: The Tel Aviv Cinematheque, 2 Shprintzak St
voyage.content: Lesbian/gay/bisexual/transgender film festival. Celebrating gender diversity. Happening in June.

voyage.name: The Tel Aviv International Student Film Festival
voyage.address: The Tel Aviv Cinematheque, 2 Shprintzak St
voyage.content: One of the world's most important student film festivals. Happening in late May.

voyage.name: Ta'am Ha'ir
voyage.content: "Taste of the City", an annual 4-day food fair, which takes place in Hayarkon Park at the beginning of summer (late May or June). Top restaurants present and sell samples of their finest dishes for special prices. The festival has been held under several names (e.g. Tel Aviv-Eat), in different locations, and sometimes in cities other than Tel Aviv. Make sure to check the details.

voyage.name: Tel Aviv University
voyage.content: The largest proper university in Israel (the Open University, though larger, is for distance learning and does not grant doctorates), situated in Ramat Aviv.

voyage.name: Tel Aviv-Jaffa Academic College
voyage.content: A smaller college in Tel Aviv

voyage.name: Afeka
voyage.content: Tel Aviv Academic College of Engineering

voyage.name: Ulpan Bayit
voyage.content: Private Hebrew language school (ulpan) in the Florentin neighbourhood, founded in 2013. Intensive, morning and evening Hebrew courses at all levels for newcomers and visitors, plus online classes.

voyage.name: Eretz Israel Museum
voyage.price: Museum/Planetarium+Museum - Adult: ₪42/74, Student & Soldier: ₪28/60, Children under 18: Free/₪32
voyage.content: History, archaeology and culture - includes the archaeological site of Tel Qasile, the remains of an early Philistine settlement. In addition the museum has a Planetarium.

voyage.name: ANU - Museum of the Jewish People
voyage.address: Tel Aviv University Campus, Klausner Street
voyage.content: This multimedia museum tells the story of the 2000 years of Jewish life throughout the entire world. It’s less about history and more about people: how the lived, worked, celebrated or prayed. A must-see if you like to know more about Jewish heritage. It was known as the Museum of Jewish Diaspora (Beth Hatefutsoth in Hebrew) until 2021, when it reopened after a remodel and re-brand.

voyage.name: Yitzhak Rabin Center
voyage.content: A museum dedicated to the life of Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin, and the political and social development of Israel as a whole. The center is involved in educational activities, which mostly help young Israelis prepare to contribute to a democratic and tolerant society.

voyage.name: Palmach Museum
voyage.content: The most interesting and gripping of Tel Aviv's military museums, it teaches the history of the Palmach, the main elite branch of Israel's military in 1948. There are no traditional exhibits, rather, you experience a 90 min interactive presentation as part of a group.

voyage.name: Steinhardt Museum of Natural History
voyage.content: Opened in summer 2018, mainly aimed at children, various fauna & flora and eco-exhibits.

voyage.name: Tel Aviv University
voyage.content: You can walk around a bit to see how the Israeli student looks like. The university gallery sometimes features interesting exhibitions. The newly built Smolarsh Auditorium is nicknamed The Atomic Reactor, due to its strange shape. The red-brick synagogue is referred to as The Petrol Distillery because its resemblance to the country main distilleries north of Haifa.

voyage.name: Israel Trade Fairs & Convention Center
voyage.content: Holds many exhibitions and events

voyage.name: Seven Flour Mills
voyage.content: A historic site including a Roman bridge, a dam, and old water mills.

voyage.name: Bird's Head
voyage.content: The confluence of the Ayalon and Yarkon rivers is located here. The land in between the rivers is shaped like a bird's head, hence the name.

voyage.name: Bird's Head Birdwatching Center
voyage.content: A landscaped birdwatching center, fittingly located on the Bird's Head peninsula.

voyage.name: Cliff beach
voyage.content: The poshest beach in Tel Aviv, where you might run into Israeli celebrities. There is a sandstone cliff running just behind the beach, and above it are sand dunes. This beach used to have an entrance fee, however that may no longer be the case.

voyage.name: Tel Baruch beach
voyage.content: Sandwiched between the sea and the Sdeh Dov domestic airport, this beach can be reached from its north end (Tsvi Propes street) or south end (Yarkon Park). It is popular with families.

voyage.name: Yarkon Park
voyage.content: The largest public park in Tel Aviv. The Yarkon River runs through the park, and spills into the Mediterranean Sea. The park is an excellent place for physical activities of all kinds - walking, jogging, cycling, kissing, etc. You can also come and join a game of football/basketball at almost any time. The park is clean (but the river is not; do not swim!) and except for a few small parts is very well lit at night. O

voyage.name: TLV Balloon
voyage.content: A balloon ride, rising to a height of 90 m over the Yarkon Park, offering a great view of the park and the Tel Aviv skyline.

voyage.name: iClimb TLV
voyage.content: A giant climbing wall.

voyage.name: SkyTown
voyage.content: A zipline park

voyage.name: Luna Park
voyage.price: ₪105, discounts for many local credit cards - ask your Israeli friends
voyage.hours: Not open every day. Check specifically
voyage.content: Tel Aviv's main amusement park. While the rides it has to offer are no competition to ones that can be found in other countries, it should still be considered for a visit by thrill-loving tourists, especially families with kids, since the park has a large amount of child-friendly rides. The park has two rollercoasters.

voyage.name: Meymadion
voyage.price: ₪105, discounts for many local credit cards - ask your Israeli friends
voyage.content: A large waterpark very close to Luna Park. It offers a varied selection of waterslides, both for thrill seekers and for children. Note that during summer vacations the lines get quite long.

voyage.name: Maccabi Tel Aviv Judo club
voyage.content: Good solid dojo

voyage.name: Ramat Aviv Mall
voyage.content: One of the biggest and most popular shopping centres in the city. You will find here all the major brands, from Tommy Hilfiger to Calvin Klein, in addition to some Israeli brands. There is also a good food court with a nice selection of fast food chains. In line with the neighborhood, this mall as a bit upscale compared to other Tel Aviv malls.

voyage.name: Shuk Tzafon
voyage.content: An indoor market. Its stalls sell raw food materials and prepared dishes. It caters to workers of the nearby Ramat HaHayal office park, as well as residents of the upscale nearby neighborhoods.

voyage.name: Frame chef & sushi bar
voyage.content: Stylish and trendy restaurant offering sushi and other Japanese and Asian dishes.

voyage.name: Avantgarde
voyage.content: American diner, with hamburgers, buffalo wings and steaks plus TV sports.

voyage.name: Giraffe Grill
voyage.content: Popular and inexpensive chain restaurant, offering many dishes from various Asian cuisines.

voyage.name: Leo Bloom's
voyage.content: The second most famous Irish pub in Tel Aviv. A meeting place for the northern Tel Aviv youth and visitors.

voyage.name: West All Suite Hotel
voyage.content: Upmarket resort hotel on the cliff above Tzuk Beach. Northern edge of city several kilometers from other attractions. Food is not kosher.

voyage.name: Rabin Square
voyage.content: The largest public square in Israel is at the footsteps of the city hall. This square hosts many public demonstrations and events, often with tens of thousands of participants in attendance. The square is named after former Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin, who was assassinated here during a peace rally in 1995. A memorial in his memory is at the northeast corner of the square.

voyage.name: Gan Meir
voyage.content: A small garden between King George and Chernihovsky streets. A green little corner in the midst of the metropolitan with a cute pond in the center and a small dog park. On some evenings you might see mature people playing kids' games - it's Tel Aviv.

voyage.name: Sarona
voyage.content: Sarona was a Templer colony founded in the late 19th century. The Templers were removed in World War II and the area continued to be used for British and later Israeli government and military offices. Today it is a shopping and entertainment district filled with restored German Templer architecture. It is known for its picturesque paths and buildings, upscale restaurants, and luxurious food market.

voyage.name: Tel Aviv Port
voyage.content: Once a commercial seaport, the Port of Tel Aviv was abandoned and later reimagined as a popular attraction and shopping district. The port is one of the most dynamic areas in Tel Aviv, including a multitude of shops, restaurants and nightclubs. During the day, this is a beautiful seaside boardwalk, great for restaurants and people-watching. At night, the bars and nightclubs open up.

voyage.name: Dizengoff Square
voyage.content: An elevated square on top of which there is a big fountain with a mix of fire and water. This is one of the known symbols of Tel Aviv. It reopened in June 2018 after renovations.

voyage.name: Habima Square
voyage.content: Home to a number of cultural institutions such as the Habima Theatre, the Culture Palace and the Helena Rubinstein Pavilion for Contemporary Art, its draw is the rectangular water feature and corresponding flower bed. In the nighttime, the square comes alive with bustling nightlife and projections against the wall of the Habima Theatre.

voyage.name: Neve Tzedek
voyage.content: A historical part of town with art galleries and restaurants.

voyage.name: Jaffa Railway Station
voyage.content: Trains no longer go here, so the station has been transformed into a popular outdoor shopping area.

voyage.name: Trumpeldor Cemetery
voyage.content: Tel Aviv's original cemetery, where many central figures from the early Zionist period and beginning of the state are buried. You can see the graves of politicians like Dizengoff, Arlozorov, and Prime Minister Moshe Sharet; writers like Bialik, Tchernikhovsky, and Ahad HaAm; singer Arik Einstein; and many others. Most of the famous graves are in a cluster at the west end of the cemetery - very obvious if you can read

voyage.name: Tel Aviv Great Synagogue
voyage.content: A large synagogue, built to be the central synagogue for Tel Aviv. But now it essentially functions as a regular neighborhood synagogue, and the neighborhood is pretty secular, so the building is vastly oversized for its current use. There is some nice artwork and stained glass windows inside. From the outside, it is badly in need of a cleaning and paint job, but the modernist arches added in 1969 are worth checking

voyage.name: Crazy House
voyage.content: A bizarre apartment building that resembles the buildings of Gaudi in Barcelona.

voyage.name: Pagoda house
voyage.content: A large private house built in 1924. Designed with the guideline that it connect Eastern and Western architecture, its elements include Muslim arches, Greek columns, and of course a pagoda.

voyage.name: Shared Villa
voyage.content: An oddball apartment building on the beach which starts normally, but then grows outward on gravity-defying columns. By architect Tzvi Harel, who drew up the design never intending to build it, until it caught the eye of a local entrepreneur.

voyage.name: Asia House
voyage.content: A seven-story office building. With oscillating wave-like layers, this is a more modern take on Tel Aviv's traditional white Bauhaus architecture.

voyage.name: David Ben Gurion on his head
voyage.content: A whimsical statue of David Ben Gurion doing one of his trademark headstands. A good photo op.

voyage.name: Altalena memorial
voyage.content: One of the most important moments in early Israeli history happened here. In 1948, David Ben Gurion ordered an attack on the Altalena ship, which was carrying arms for the splinter Irgun militia. Irgun leader Menachem Begin commanded his troops not to defend themselves, believing that nothing could be worse for the new state than a civil war. There is a small memorial here to the 16 Irgun fighters who were killed in

voyage.name: Independence Hall
voyage.content: In accordance with its name, Independence Hall is the place where the Israeli Declaration of Independence was proclaimed by David Ben-Gurion on 14 May 1948, thus officially establishing the modern State of Israel. Though essentially nondescript on the outside; inside, visitors can see the actual hall itself, watch a short documentary film, and view several artifacts in the small museum.

voyage.name: Tel Aviv Museum of Art
voyage.content: The city's main art gallery focuses on modern and contemporary work. Changing exhibitions are housed here, in the Rubinstein Pavilion and in the Amir Building. (Enter via the Amir as the main frontage and entrance are being rebuilt.) The children's basement is great fun and not just for kids. Within the same complex is the Golda Meir Center of Performing Arts, hosting opera, ballet, and theatre (see "Do"). The city l

voyage.name: Helena Rubinstein Pavilion
voyage.content: Displays temporary exhibitions from the nearby Museum of Art. Same hours, free entry with museum ticket.

voyage.name: Bauhaus Center Tel Aviv
voyage.content: Despite its compact size, it manages to survey almost the entire gamut of the Bauhaus design genre. Detailed exhibitions, books, maps and posters, multimedia and a great little shop. The center also conducts tours of the Tel Aviv Bauhaus White City (F 10AM, duration 2 hours, book ahead) and other destinations.

voyage.name: Ben-Gurion House
voyage.content: Home of Prime Minister David Ben Gurion from 1931-1968, and the place where Israel's Declaration of Independence was written. Now it is a museum focusing on Ben Gurion's life.

voyage.name: Gutman Art Museum
voyage.content: Focuses on the work of painter and sculptor Nachum Gutman.

voyage.name: Joseph Bau House
voyage.content: A museum run by the daughters of Joseph Bau, an artist who saved many lives during the Holocaust and is featured in the movie "Schindler's List". The daughters give an original and uplifting presentation describing their parents' lives in the context of the Holocaust.

voyage.name: Rokach House
voyage.content: A house built in 1887 in Neve Tzedek, at a time when this neighborhood was still considered part of Jaffa, and Tel Aviv did not yet exist. It has been restored to its original condition, and you can tour it and learn about the history of Neve Tzedek and Jewish settlement outside the old city of Jaffa.

voyage.name: Museum of Illusions
voyage.content: A museum of optical illusions, including fun 3D ones like the Ames room that you can walk into.

voyage.name: Museum of the History of Tel Aviv-Yafo
voyage.content: A city history museum, housed in the old City Hall building.

voyage.name: Bialik House
voyage.content: Home of Hayim Nahman Bialik, Israel's national poet. Now a museum dedicated to Bialik's life.

voyage.name: Rubin Museum of Art
voyage.content: An exhibition of the art of Israeli painter Reuven Rubin.

voyage.name: Haganah Museum
voyage.content: Recounting the fascinating story of the embryonic Israel Defence Force, from British Mandate days to Israeli independence in 1948 and beyond, lots of interesting artifacts, weapons and memorabilia.

voyage.name: Jabotinsky Institute
voyage.content: Small museum all about the life of Ze'ev Jabotinsky. Features a film about a clandestine immigration operation and a few cases showing his personal effects.

voyage.name: Etzel museum
voyage.content: Very detailed history of the Etzel (Irgun) movement and their operations, also includes a short film. This museum tells the overall story of Etzel starting in the 1930s and ending in 1948.

voyage.name: Etzel 1948 museum
voyage.content: A separate museum which focuses on Etzel/Irgun military operations in 1948, especially the conquest of northern Jaffa, including the current location of this museum.

voyage.name: Former Israel Defense Forces History Museum
voyage.content: This used to be a museum of old military vehicles, but in 2019 the contents were moved to Yad LaShiryon museum in Latrun. It's mentioned here so that you don't mistakenly visit it based on old recommendations from elsewhere.

voyage.name: Metzitzim beach
voyage.content: Just south of Tel Aviv Port (which has no beach, the waves crash against the wall of the boardwalk). This beach became famous as the setting of the movie Metzitzim (1972). Now it's the most popular destination for families.

voyage.name: Separate beach
voyage.content: This beach is male-only on Sunday/Tuesday/Thursday and female-only on Monday/Wednesday/Friday. On Saturdays it's open to everyone. It attracts many religious people who don't want to be seen by the opposite sex in bathing attire. It's surrounded by a wall to prevent people outside from looking.

voyage.name: Dog beach
voyage.content: A narrow strip of beach, south of the separate beach, where dogs are permitted.

voyage.name: Hilton beach
voyage.content: A meeting place for Tel Aviv's LGBT community.

voyage.name: Surfers' beach
voyage.content: Just south of Hilton beach, the waves off this narrow beach are popular with surfers.

voyage.name: Gordon beach
voyage.content: Full of beach volleyball courts, exercise equipment, and other sports facilities.

voyage.name: Frishman beach
voyage.content: A very busy beach with a heavy presence of French speakers. Also known for the elderly locals who come here early in the mornings to exercise.

voyage.name: Bograshov beach
voyage.content: A beach that heavily attracts Tel Aviv residents, and is quieter than some of the other beaches in town.

voyage.name: Jerusalem beach
voyage.content: The biggest destination for teenagers, who find it easy to get here from the nearby Carmel Market bus terminal. Opposite Allenby street, it was renamed in 1987 in honor of Jerusalem.

voyage.name: Aviv beach
voyage.alt: Tel Aviv beach, Dolphinarium beach, Tupim beach, Banana Drum beach
voyage.content: The beach has an Eastern vibe, with yoga, tai chi, and drum circles taking place at various hours of the day.

voyage.name: Alma beach
voyage.content: There is no breakwater here, which makes the waves bigger and more dangerous, and fewer people go into the water here. However, this is Tel Aviv's most beautiful beach, with a nice view of Old Jaffa. At sundown, you can see brides and grooms who come here to take pictures together.

voyage.name: Azrieli Center Lookout
voyage.content: Head to the Azrieli Center to see Tel Aviv from above. This complex with its three geometrical skyscrapers (with circle, square, and triangle footprints) is a graphical icon of the city. The bottom 3 floors contain a full-size and very popular shopping mall. But we've come here in order to climb up to the 49th floor of the circular tower, from which, they say, you can see on a good day as far as to Haifa. There’s als

voyage.name: Golda Meir Center of Performing Arts
voyage.content: Hosts opera, ballet, theatre, and concerts.

voyage.name: The Yarqon Park
voyage.content: The largest public park in Tel Aviv. The Yarqon River runs through the park, and spills into the Mediterranean Sea. Most of the park lies north of the river, but the south bank has a nice portion of it as well. The park is an excellent place for physical activities of all kinds - walking, jogging, cycling, boating, kissing, etc. You can also come and join a game of football/basketball at almost any time. The park is

voyage.name: Segway tour
voyage.content: Meeting at the Tel Aviv Port, you can ride a Segway through the Yarkon park or along the Tel Aviv beach. No experience necessary. Must reserve in advance.

voyage.name: Tel Aviv Marina
voyage.content: A port for yachts, sailing boats, and other small craft. (Not to be confused with the "Tel Aviv Port", which no longer functions as a port.) At the marina, you can engage in diving, sailing, and other water activities. There are also a few restaurants, and of course it's right next to the beach.

voyage.name: Tel Aviv Rollers
voyage.content: The hottest inline skating group in the country! Every Tuesday 50 to 250 inline skaters of all ages gather around in the parking lot in front of Ha'Bima theater in Tel Aviv at 22:00. The departure is at 22:30 for a nightskating on Tel Aviv's roads.

voyage.name: Hithavut
voyage.content: Israel's secular and religious sides meet in this venue, which sort of a cross between a synagogue and a nightclub, and hosts religious classes as well as concerts, drinking, and dancing.

voyage.name: Tel Aviv Cinematheque
voyage.content: cinematheque and movie archive with 5 cinema halls and space for watching movies from its archives. The Cinematheque screens Israeli and foreign films, and private events. Film festivals include held at the cinematheque include TLVFest, "Doc Aviv" Documentary Film Festival, "Moments of French Cinema", an Australian Film Festival and more. Its lobby hosts photo exhibitions by Israeli artists. The current building was

voyage.name: Shenkin St.
voyage.content: A trendy and much livelier street that has mainly clothing shops of smaller less known designers along with known brands. Also contains many coffee shops and restaurants. During Friday this street is as crowded on the sidewalk as most of Tel Aviv is on the road.

voyage.name: Dizengoff St.
voyage.content: Many different shops all along Dizengoff street, with the north of Dizengoff is spread with many small Israeli designer shops.

voyage.name: Ben Yehuda St.
voyage.content: A street that is close to the beach and tourist area has several Judaica, Jewelery and Souvenir shops.

voyage.name: Nachalat Binyamin St.
voyage.content: Offers tiny stores selling everything from cheap household accessories like clothes hangers and ironing boards, to specialist kosher butchers and cheese stores.

voyage.name: Kikar HaMedina
voyage.content: One of the biggest squares in Tel Aviv (and Israel). A very expensive and chic area for shopping with many major designer stores all around a big green circular traffic square.

voyage.name: Carmel Market
voyage.content: The largest and most famous market in Tel Aviv. Hosting clothing, food, souvenirs, and other shops. Watch out for the prices, not seldomly prices double for tourists.

voyage.name: Nachalat Binyamin arts and crafts fair
voyage.content: A craft fair is held in the Nachalat Binyamin pedestrian zone every Tuesday and Friday (often more frequently during the summer and other holidays). In addition to the truly original crafts (which can make good gifts), presented by their creators, you can enjoy a good atmosphere and street shows.

voyage.name: Dizengoff Antiques Market
voyage.alt: Tel Aviv Antiques and Secondhand Goods Market
voyage.content: Held twice a week in Dizengoff Square, this is a good place to find all sorts of vintage and second-hand goods.

voyage.name: Azriely Center
voyage.content: Situated at the feet of the Azriely Towers and connected to HaShalom Train Station. This is the largest mall in the city and is often over crowded. Visitors can climb to the top of the mall for a nice free view of the city, or get to the observatory at the top of the Circular Tower (see in the "do" section). There are many stores in the mall, along with a large movie theater.

voyage.name: Dizengoff Center
voyage.content: The first mall in Israel. This large mall has, in addition to the usual selection, some specialty shops, such as musical instruments, stamps, hand-held devices, hobby etc. On Thursday and Friday there is a food market inside the mall with all kinds of restaurants and amateur chefs selling dishes for decent prices.

voyage.name: Gan Ha'ir
voyage.content: Just off Rabin Square, an up-market oriented mini-mall with a great cafe at the top of it.

voyage.name: TLV Fashion Mall
voyage.content: A new shopping mall that mainly focuses on fashion. Located where the former wholesale market was.

voyage.name: Daffodil 11
voyage.content: One of the cities best second hand clothing shops. Sells modern, trendy clothing at unbelievably low prices.

voyage.name: Sipur Pashut book shop
voyage.content: Founded in 2003 by Neve Tzedek residents, the Sipur Pashut Book Shop is counted among Israel’s outstanding, independent bookshops. Sipur Pashut holds a vast English collection.

voyage.name: Gordon Gallery
voyage.content: Contemporary art by local artists.

voyage.name: Sommer Gallery
voyage.content: Young contemporary art by Israeli and international artists.

voyage.name: Gallery 97 Tel Aviv
voyage.content: Located in the heart of Tel Aviv, Gallery97 specializes in superior quality Israeli and Jewish art. A modern art gallery, concentrating on purchasing and selling artworks from Ecole de Paris and Jewish artists of the 20th century.

voyage.name: Egozi Gallery
voyage.content: Gallery and an auction house for art and antiques.

voyage.name: Humus - the son of the Syrian
voyage.content: A great hummus restaurant in the Kerem. Don't be frightened by his angry facial expression; he's always like that.

voyage.name: Bar Gurion
voyage.content: Sandwiches street bar

voyage.name: Abu Adham
voyage.content: One of the best hummus places in Tel Aviv

voyage.name: Hummus Abu Dabi
voyage.content: Small laid back vegan hummus place. It's open onto the street so it's a great place to have lunch and watch the locals as they rush by while you relax to the sound of Reggae. Fridays tend to be especially crowded.

voyage.name: Rustico
voyage.content: Great long-established Italian restaurant.

voyage.name: Tony Vespa
voyage.content: Tasty and affordable Pizzeria. The Pizza is made in the style of Rome with a thick crust, many kinds of toppings, and is paid for according to weight. Great place for a late night snack.

voyage.name: Streets
voyage.content: Popular and stylish street side cafe. It's open 24/7 and offers some good dishes as well.

voyage.name: Messa
voyage.content: Upscale restaurant, European and Mediterranean cuisine.

voyage.name: Onami
voyage.content: Japanese restaurant, mostly sushi and fish. Alongside is "Oban Koban" street-style food.

voyage.name: Four One Six
voyage.content: Vegan restaurant.

voyage.name: The 11th Floor Restaurant
voyage.address: Crown Plaza City Center Hotel, Azrieli Towers
voyage.content: The 11th Floor Restaurant has views of the cityscape of Tel Aviv. This restaurant has a spacious setting and creative dishes, recalling the finest New York restaurants. Chef Eitan Mizrahi has created an outstanding kosher menu.

voyage.name: Rosa Parks
voyage.content: A small but crowded little bar, named for the African American civil rights activist.

voyage.name: 223 Bar
voyage.content: Cocktail bar with music.

voyage.name: Ozen Bar
voyage.content: Rock bar and venue. There are 2 shows nightly by the hottest local indie bands and even the occasional party. It's right above Haozen Hashlishit (The Third Ear) store.

voyage.name: Mike's Place
voyage.content: An American-style bar features live music every night of the week. Also features outdoor seating in the more pleasant weather, pool table and televised sporting events. Mostly Anglo 20-30 something crowd, very good bar with several kinds of beer on tap.

voyage.name: Mendalimos
voyage.content: An Israeli pub and dance-bar. This is where a lot of the locals go to just to grab a beer or to enjoy the nightlife scene. Vintage design indoors, alongside outdoor balcony in which all the most important sports games are broadcast. Trendiest music from abroad and Israel.

voyage.name: Molly Bloom's Irish Pub
voyage.content: The first Irish pub in Tel Aviv, great atmosphere and reasonable prices, busy at weekends. Has food and outdoor seating. Often many UK and Irish customers, strangely enough. Molly has another branch at 6 Aluf Albert Mendler St near HaShalom station. But no relation to Leo Bloom's Bar in the Ziv Tower out in the north city; fittingly so, since Molly's main problem with Leo was the "no relation".

voyage.name: Cheers
voyage.content: Bar with mostly good reviews. Israeli timekeeping: happy hour is from opening to 22:00.

voyage.name: Temptation
voyage.content: A dark 2-floor dance-bar with mainly hip-hop music. Tuesday is karaoke night.

voyage.name: Chaser
voyage.content: Mixed reviews, expensive.

voyage.name: The Minzar
voyage.content: A bar for drinking while planning the next revolution. A very established Tel Aviv institution that's highly popular with students of humanities at Tel Aviv University.

voyage.name: Salon Berlin
voyage.content: Laid back bar and trendy clothing store. When the hipsters tire of mingling at HaProzdor, they walk down here to sit down and chill with their friends. During daytime you may also check out the clothing store next door which boasts its own trendy clothing line.

voyage.name: abraXas
voyage.content: Good food & music.

voyage.name: Lima
voyage.content: Mainly a hip-hop dance-bar with an outside area. Attracts a diverse crowd, from suburban party girls to highbrow philosophy students.

voyage.name: Flame
voyage.content: A small dark pick-up bar with a very friendly atmosphere. Tuesday nights: 1 + 1 on drinks.

voyage.name: HaShoftim
voyage.content: Classic wooden bar with stout on tap and outdoor seating as well.

voyage.name: Shalvata
voyage.content: Coffee shop, bar-restaurant, on the beach

voyage.name: Dancing Camel Brewing Company
voyage.content: Tel Aviv's only microbrewery and Israel's oldest continually operating microbrewery. Featuring 16 types of hand-crafted beers brewed on premises. Always an interesting seasonal beer or two (try the Golem - an Iced IPA at 11.3% on tap every full moon). Bar extends into the brewery so you can sit only a few feet from the copper brewhouse. Live Blues on Monday nights, Jazz on Tuesday nights. During Football season enjoy

voyage.name: Alma De Cuba
voyage.content: Cuban bar & lounge. Salsa dance club.

voyage.name: Crown Sea Hostel
voyage.content: Clean friendly hostel by Ge'ula beach.

voyage.name: Little Tel Aviv Hostel
voyage.content: Clean friendly hostel not far from the bus station.

voyage.name: Abraham Hostel Tel Aviv
voyage.content: Gets good reviews for vibe, cleanliness and location.

voyage.name: Gordon Inn
voyage.content: Guest house with 7 private rooms, no dorm, very basic but comfy. Close to the beach.

voyage.name: Hayarkon Hostel
voyage.content: Close to beach but very uneven quality.

voyage.name: Beachfront Hostel
voyage.content: Handy for beachfront, gets mixed reviews for quality of accommodation.

voyage.name: Momo's Hostel
voyage.price: Dorm bed from ₪90, private room from ₪200
voyage.content: Rooms small and a bit dated, rated only 3.2 out of 5, but good value for such a central location.

voyage.name: Dizengoff Suites Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: Boutique hotel with 5 suites, no single rooms, long rentals available.

voyage.name: Bell Hotel
voyage.content: Near the beach, short walk from centre. Rooms are small, the "spa" is just a dry sauna, and there's quite a bit of street noise.

voyage.name: Artist Hotel
voyage.content: A combined art museum/hotel, original modern art fills the entire hotel. Central location. Part of Atlas chain.

voyage.name: Golden Beach Hotel
voyage.content: On Tel Aviv beachfront, 1 km north of Jaffa. Okay for comfort.

voyage.name: Sun City Hotel
voyage.content: Clean & friendly, handy for beach, Sheinkin St., the arts and crafts fair at Nahalat Binyamin & Bezalel Market.

voyage.name: Armon Hayarkon
voyage.content: Mid-range hotel, they usually score well for comfort, cleanliness and service.

voyage.name: Cinema Hotel Tel Aviv
voyage.content: Located in a restored 1930 Bauhaus building, the Esther Cinema. Rooms and public areas are decorated with a cinema theme - they've done this with real pizzazz. Breakfast is excellent.

voyage.name: Leonardo Beach Hotel
voyage.content: On the sea shore promenade. Has a great view of the marina.

voyage.name: Prima Tel Aviv
voyage.content: A 4-star, boutique hotel across from the beach.

voyage.name: Grand Beach Hotel
voyage.content: Spacious, renovated rooms, and stylish urban design. Each room is equipped with a mini fridge, LCD television and cable, and personal safe. A spacious pool and sunbathing area on the roof of the hotel has panoramic view of the seashore and the city.

voyage.name: Vital Hotel Tel Aviv
voyage.content: Boutique hotel. An elevator connects the hotel with the new shopping mall and cafes at Weizmann Center.

voyage.name: Hotel de la Mer
voyage.content: Boutique hotel in a Bauhaus building, rooms in a minimalist style. No breakfast on site, you get a voucher for the cafe a short block away. They also run the Olympia 500 m north along the street.

voyage.name: Ana Bnei Dan Hostel
voyage.content: 45 rooms all with a/c.

voyage.name: The Lusky
voyage.content: Clean friendly place, free parking, most rooms have kitchenettes.

voyage.name: Maxim Hotel Tel Aviv
voyage.content: Friendly hotel within a minute of the beach, rooms are small.

voyage.name: Savoy Hotel Sea-Side Tel Aviv
voyage.content: Barely 60 m from beach, nice rooms but a tad small. Great sunset views from rooftop terrace but this is a smoking area.

voyage.name: Tal Hotel Tel Aviv
voyage.content: Good hotel within walking distance of the nightlife, beach and Dizengoff. Part of Atlas chain who have a dozen hotels in TA.

voyage.name: Pink House Tel Aviv
voyage.address: 17 Raban Gamliel st. (corner with 10 Nagara st.)
voyage.content: The only gay guest house in Israel. It is in the heart of Tel Aviv gay and center district and a short walk to the beach. Best to book in advance.

voyage.name: Shalom Hotel & Relax
voyage.content: Boutique hotel near the marina, gets great reviews for comfort and service.

voyage.name: Alexander Tel Aviv Hotel
voyage.content: Boutique-style hotel with suites in contemporary style.

voyage.name: Carlton Tel Aviv
voyage.content: Next to marina, some construction noise, but generally a good standard for rooms and service.

voyage.name: Crowne Plaza Tel Aviv
voyage.content: Good location by marina, okay rooms, but a lot of noisy construction all day long - the end date for this isn't known.

voyage.name: Dan Panorama Tel Aviv
voyage.content: Beachfront hotel gets great reviews for comfort, food and service.

voyage.name: Dan Tel Aviv Hotel
voyage.content: Boxy modern hotel on the shoreline. Quality of rooms varies greatly depending on whether they've been upgraded yet: this work continues in early 2020.

voyage.name: Intercontinental David Tel Aviv
voyage.content: Great location near beach, decent rooms showing their age. Service mostly good with some lapses.

voyage.name: Hilton Tel Aviv
voyage.content: Large hotel on northern seafront. Rooms okay but showing their age, service erratic.

voyage.name: Sheraton Tel Aviv
voyage.content: A high-class international chain hotel, overlooking the Med; part of the Marriott chain and fairly reliable for comfort.

voyage.name: Crowne Plaza City Center Tel Aviv
voyage.content: In the Azrieli tower complex 2 km from sea, reliable chain offering.

voyage.name: Isrotel Tower Hotel
voyage.content: Good location and rooms, try for a sea view else all you see is surrounding construction. The roof-top pool is neat. Parking is problematic but that's typical for downtown TA.

voyage.name: The Drisco Hotel
voyage.content: The Drisco Hotel is in the center of the picturesque and pastoral American – German colony in Tel Aviv which was established in 1866, with a quiet and pleasant environment surrounded by beautiful houses which were restored by an artist. The George and John restaurant, headed by chef Tomer Tal, won the title "the best restaurant in Israel" and made it into the top 6 in the ranking of the best restaurants of "Middle Ea

voyage.name: Florentin neighborhood
voyage.content: A previously run-down but beautiful area, which is now gentrifying. Full of old, often colourful, Bauhaus buildings in various states of disrepair, however many of them are being renovated and restored to something approximating their former glory. The area is being completely redeveloped, and some construction of new apartment blocks is also taking place. This has caused some controversy with the locals who want to

voyage.name: Lehi Museum
voyage.content: A museum describing the right-wing Lehi militia which operated between 1940-1948. This building was the hiding place of Lehi leader Avraham Stern when he was killed by British police in 1942.

voyage.name: Artist Workshops
voyage.content: For those with a passion for street art or an alternative hippie or punky side, this small quarter of artist workshops is covered with unusual, colourful, surrealistic, and political high-quality graffiti.

voyage.name: Levinsky Market
voyage.address: Levinski Street, between Hertzl St. and Ha'aliya Street
voyage.content: An extremely colorful outside market boasting a variety of spice shops and ethnic restaurants.

voyage.name: St. Peter's Church
voyage.content: Russian orthodox church, built in 1894.

voyage.name: Water ski
voyage.content: Wakeboarding and waterskiing, for amateurs and experts. Open all year round, but it might be unpleasantly cold in winter.

voyage.name: Yad Eliyahu arena
voyage.alt: Menora Mivtachim Arena, previously Nokia Arena
voyage.content: This arena is home to the Maccabi Tel Aviv basketball team. Tickets can be bought from the team's web site.

voyage.name: Graffiti tour
voyage.content: A number of tour guides offer tours of the graffiti and urban culture in the Florentin neighborhood. (Don't worry, despite the graffiti this neighborhood is perfectly safe.)

voyage.name: Levinsky Market
voyage.content: The best place in Tel Aviv to buy spices, dried fruits, and different kinds of legume. This small market is stretched along Levinsky Street.

voyage.name: Hatikva Market
voyage.content: The most "authentic", non-gentrified market in Tel Aviv. A good place to find Iraqi-Jewish cuisine, as well as the usual fruits and vegetables and other market staples.

voyage.name: 24 Rupi
voyage.content: Exemplifying the south Tel Aviv notion of chic, this is an Indian guest house-type restaurant/lounge established by Israelis enchanted by the India vibe, serving Tali and other Indian dishes.

voyage.name: Casbah
voyage.content: A laid back, indoor/outdoor spot with good indie music, Moroccan inspired dishes, and WiFi.

voyage.name: City Break
voyage.content: Coffee shop serving great sandwiches with bread freshly made on the premises, cakes and salads. Herzl and Florentin Street.

voyage.name: Dixie
voyage.content: One of the first restaurants in Tel Aviv famous for being open 24/7, serves American food, including steaks, hamburgers and an excellent side-dish named home-fries.

voyage.name: Florentin 10
voyage.content: Coffee shop and restaurant by day (check out their business lunches), bar by night. Florentin Street.

voyage.name: Hummus Beit Leichem
voyage.content: Vegetarian, kosher hummus restaurant on the corner of Florentin and Vital Streets.

voyage.name: Hummus Eliyahu
voyage.content: Very delicious warm hummus with chickpeas, tahina and/or fava beans. Basic meal includes a refill, but it's not comparable to the Subway Coke refill you are used to in Europe.

voyage.name: Lenny's
voyage.content: A popular coffee shop and (at night) bar. Vital Street.

voyage.name: Perla
voyage.content: Slightly more upmarket (but not much), beautifully designed modern bar/ restaurant. Florentin Street.

voyage.name: The Salon
voyage.content: Expensive but worth it.

voyage.name: Yoko Sushi Bar
voyage.content: Eat a quick snack of freshly-made sushi. Florentin Street.

voyage.name: Block Club
voyage.content: Usually open Th and F nights and featuring big name international DJs weekly.

voyage.name: Duplex Club
voyage.content: 3 venues club

voyage.name: Havana Club
voyage.content: Latin music and salsa club.

voyage.name: Udna
voyage.content: A great, chilled-out pub.

voyage.name: Florentine Backpackers Hostel
voyage.content: Party hostel, good for young solos as they get everyone eating and drinking together then hit the pubs, but quiet time after 23:00.

voyage.name: Overstay Hostel TLV
voyage.content: Basic hostel 1 km from beach, sometimes noisy, but they mostly keep on top of the cleaning. They've another hostel nominally in Jaffa, but just the other side of the park.

voyage.name: Florentin House
voyage.content: This hostel gets great reviews for comfort, cleanliness and service. Dorm plus private rooms.

voyage.name: Jaffa Clock Tower
voyage.content: A local landmark, built in 1903.

voyage.name: Immanuel Church
voyage.content: Protestant church built in 1904.

voyage.name: Saint Anthony of Padua Catholic Church
Presbyterian Saint Peter Church
voyage.content: Built in the 1930s but abandoned since 1948, this church is generally not accessible to visit.

voyage.name: Old Jaffa and port
voyage.content: One of the oldest ports in the world, and formerly the biggest seaport in Israel. This is the point where Jonah reputedly boarded a ship and was later swallowed by a big fish. Today the port and the area close to it have become a quaint, interesting renovated district. The port holds various shops, restaurants and events. See websites for Jaffa port and Old Jaffa.

voyage.name: Old Jaffa Museum
voyage.content: This complex, built in the 13th century, was the Ottoman government headquarters. It is used for art exhibitions.

voyage.name: Ramesses Gate
voyage.content: Archaeological remains from the 16th century BCE which can be freely viewed. However, they are hard to appreciate without a tour guide.

voyage.name: Zodiac alleys
voyage.content: A network of restored alleys, full of art galleries, which lead to the Jaffa seaport. The alleys are named after the signs of the zodiac.

voyage.name: Andromeda's rock
voyage.content: The rock in Jaffa harbor to which, according to Greek myth, Andromeda was tied before being rescued by Perseus.

voyage.name: Wishing Bridge
voyage.content: The myth says if you touch your zodiac sign and face the sea, your wish will come true.

voyage.name: al-Bahr Sea Mosque
voyage.content: Built in 1675, this is the oldest surviving mosque in Jaffa. Due to its proximity to the sea, it is still used by fishermen and sailors, as it has been for centuries.

voyage.name: St. Peter's Catholic Church
voyage.content: A Franciscan church, built in the 19th century on the remains of Crusaders' fortress, which serves also as a hostel. It is said that Napoleon stayed in that church while it was a hostel.

voyage.name: Saint Nicholas Monastery
voyage.content: Armenian monastery at least a 1,000 years old.

voyage.name: Saint Archangel Michael Monastery
voyage.content: Greek Orthodox church, the original building dating back to the 17th century was destroyed in a fire in 1963. It was rebuilt in 1994.

voyage.name: St. George's Church
voyage.content: Greek Orthodox church.

voyage.name: Givat HaAliyah beach
voyage.content: The quietest of Tel Aviv's beaches, and the only one you where are likely to find free parking nearby.

voyage.name: Bloomfield Stadium
voyage.content: Home to Tel Aviv's three football (soccer) clubs - Maccabi Tel Aviv, Hapoel Tel Aviv, and Bnei Yehuda Tel Aviv.

voyage.name: Nalaga’at Theater
voyage.content: A theatrical performance performed entirely by deaf-blind people (with dual disability). Includes elements of circus arts and sign language, as well as regular theater.

voyage.name: Wheel Bee Bike Rental
voyage.content: Wheel Bee offers various kinds of bikes for rent, electric & regular, for all ages.

voyage.name: House of Clues
voyage.price: 222 NIS per person, 383 NIS for two
voyage.address: The Container House, Jaffa Port, Pier 3, floor 2
voyage.content: Guided inner journeys in a video dome, with Vision Art and music. The Journey Through the Chakras is held in English and lasts 75 minutes.

voyage.name: Flea Market and Bazaar
voyage.content: An outdoor market where you can buy almost anything for low prices. Especially good for antiques.

voyage.name: Abouelafia and Sons
voyage.content: The most famous bakery in Tel Aviv-Jaffa, if not in the entire country. Mounds of pastries and confectioneries. Israelis drive for miles to visit this bakery.

voyage.name: Aladin
voyage.content: Seafood, great location, food gets mixed reviews.

voyage.name: Ali Karavan Abu Hassan
voyage.hours: Sun-Fri 07:45-14:45 or until the hummus runs out
voyage.content: Famous for its hummus, massabaha (coarsely textured hummus with whole chick peas), and ful (cooked spicy fava beans). Many Israelis claim it to be the best Hummus in Israel.

voyage.name: Blackout
voyage.content: At this restaurant you eat a meal entirely in the dark, simulating the experience of blind people. Part of the Nalaga’at Center which works with blind and deaf people (see "Do" section above). Prior reservations are needed.

voyage.name: Itzik HaGadol
voyage.price: ₪200 steaks, 2 skewers with meat ₪80. Salads ₪28 with a meal
voyage.content: You get the table filled with an amazing number of salad dishes. Then you get a great steak, kebab or meat on skewers.

voyage.name: Goldman
voyage.content: Breakfast, lunch, or dinner with a view of the beach end old Jaffa.

voyage.name: Cafe Puaa
voyage.content: Mainstay for Israeli food, especially breakfast/brunch/lunch. Local favorite for their fried cauliflower.

voyage.name: Onza
voyage.content: Popular upscale modern Middle Eastern dinners with Turkish flair. Lunch also F & Sa. Reservations recommended.

voyage.name: Shmone
voyage.content: A very beautiful place located in an old Jaffa-style building, it's kind of a private membership club with many older richer people that the usual hangout.

voyage.name: Saloona
voyage.content: A local neighborhood bar with an art orientation. Often art of local artists is presented on the walls.

voyage.name: Leo 5
voyage.content: Located beneath the Ilana Goor Museum on the top of the hill, this bar is a great place to hang out. The owner is most generous and boasts a wide array of rock and roll memorabilia. You'll probably be able to hear the bar before you see it.

voyage.name: Old Jaffa Hostel
voyage.content: In the heart of the flea market, a shabby-chic place. Can be noisy from nearby bars.

voyage.name: Milk & Honey Hostel
voyage.content: Friendly but basic hostel in a good location.
